title: Male Reproductive System
content:
# Male Reproductive System

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Identify the main structures of the male reproductive system
- Describe the functions of each structure
- Explain how sperm are produced and transported
- Describe the structure and function of sperm cells

## Introduction

The **male reproductive system** is designed to produce, store, and deliver sperm cells (male gametes). Understanding the anatomy and function of this system is essential for understanding human reproduction and related health topics.

## Key Concepts

### Overview of Male Reproductive System

**Main functions:**
- Produce sperm (male gametes)
- Produce testosterone (male hormone)
- Deliver sperm to female reproductive system

[DIAGRAM: Male reproductive system showing all structures]

### Structures and Functions

| Structure | Function |
|-----------|----------|
| Testes | Produce sperm and testosterone |
| Scrotum | Holds testes outside body; temperature regulation |
| Epididymis | Stores and matures sperm |
| Sperm duct (vas deferens) | Transports sperm from testes |
| Seminal vesicles | Produce fluid for semen |
| Prostate gland | Produces fluid for semen |
| Urethra | Carries semen (and urine) out of body |
| Penis | Delivers semen into female |

### The Testes

**Structure:**
- Pair of oval organs
- Located in scrotum (outside body cavity)
- Contain seminiferous tubules
- Contain interstitial cells (Leydig cells)

**Functions:**
1. Produce sperm (in seminiferous tubules)
2. Produce testosterone (in Leydig cells)

**Why outside the body?**
- Sperm production requires lower temperature
- ~35°C (not 37°C body temperature)
- Scrotum regulates temperature

### Sperm Production (Spermatogenesis)

**Location:** Seminiferous tubules in testes

**Process:**
1. Germ cells in tubule walls
2. Cells divide by mitosis (diploid)
3. Cells divide by meiosis (haploid)
4. Cells develop into sperm
5. Takes about 70 days

**Numbers:**
- ~300 million sperm produced per day
- Continuous from puberty throughout life

### Sperm Structure

| Part | Structure | Function |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Head | Contains nucleus | Carries genetic material (haploid) |
| Acrosome | Enzyme-containing cap | Breaks through egg membranes |
| Midpiece | Packed with mitochondria | Provides energy for movement |
| Tail (flagellum) | Long, whip-like | Propels sperm forward |

[DIAGRAM: Structure of a sperm cell]

### Sperm Adaptations

| Adaptation | How it helps |
|------------|-------------|
| Streamlined shape | Moves efficiently through fluid |
| Tail (flagellum) | Swimming movement |
| Many mitochondria | ATP for tail movement |
| Acrosome enzymes | Penetrate egg |
| Haploid nucleus | Correct chromosome number after fertilisation |
| Small size | Many can be produced |
| No cytoplasm storage | Lightweight for movement |

### The Epididymis

**Location:** Coiled tube on back of testis

**Functions:**
- Stores sperm (2-3 weeks)
- Sperm mature and gain motility
- Absorbs dead sperm

### Sperm Duct (Vas Deferens)

**Structure:** Muscular tube

**Function:**
- Carries sperm from epididymis
- Muscular walls contract during ejaculation
- Joins with ducts from seminal vesicles

**Vasectomy:** Cutting vas deferens for male sterilisation

### Accessory Glands

**Seminal vesicles:**
- Produce ~60% of semen volume
- Fluid contains fructose (energy for sperm)
- Contains prostaglandins (stimulate female tract)

**Prostate gland:**
- Produces ~30% of semen volume
- Slightly alkaline fluid
- Neutralises acidic vagina
- Contains enzymes

**Cowper's glands:**
- Small amount of lubricating fluid
- Pre-ejaculatory fluid

### Semen Composition

| Component | Source | Function |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Sperm | Testes | Fertilisation |
| Fructose | Seminal vesicles | Energy for sperm |
| Alkaline fluid | Prostate | Neutralise vaginal acid |
| Enzymes | Prostate | Aid sperm movement |
| Prostaglandins | Seminal vesicles | Stimulate contractions |

**Volume:** 2-5 mL per ejaculation
**Sperm count:** 40-300 million per mL

### Testosterone

**Produced by:** Leydig cells in testes

**Functions:**
- Stimulates sperm production
- Development of male secondary sexual characteristics
- Maintains male reproductive system
- Affects behaviour and mood

**Secondary sexual characteristics:**
- Deeper voice
- Facial and body hair
- Increased muscle mass
- Broadening of shoulders

### The Penis

**Structure:**
- Contains erectile tissue
- Fills with blood during arousal
- Urethra runs through centre

**Function:**
- Delivers sperm into female vagina
- Also passes urine (separate function)

## Common Exam Questions

- Name the parts of the male reproductive system
- Describe the function of testes
- Explain adaptations of sperm for their function
- Describe the role of accessory glands

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** Sperm are stored in the testes
- **Reality:** Sperm are stored in the epididymis

- **Misconception:** Semen and sperm are the same thing
- **Reality:** Semen contains sperm plus fluids from glands

- **Misconception:** Testes produce sperm continuously from birth
- **Reality:** Sperm production begins at puberty

- **Misconception:** All sperm are healthy and functional
- **Reality:** Many sperm are abnormal; only healthy ones can fertilise

## Practice Questions

1. Name the organ that produces sperm. (1 mark)

2. State two functions of the testes. (2 marks)

3. Describe three adaptations of sperm cells for their function. (3 marks)

4. Explain why the testes are located outside the body. (2 marks)

5. Describe the role of the seminal vesicles and prostate gland. (4 marks)

6. Describe the journey of sperm from where they are produced to where they leave the body, naming all the structures involved. (4 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Testis | Male gonad; produces sperm and testosterone |
| Scrotum | Sac holding testes outside body |
| Epididymis | Tube where sperm mature and are stored |
| Vas deferens | Tube carrying sperm from epididymis |
| Semen | Fluid containing sperm and secretions |
| Testosterone | Male sex hormone |
| Spermatogenesis | Process of sperm production |
| Acrosome | Enzyme-containing cap on sperm head |

## Summary

- Testes produce sperm and testosterone
- Located in scrotum (cooler temperature needed)
- Sperm have head (nucleus, acrosome), midpiece (mitochondria), tail
- Epididymis stores and matures sperm
- Vas deferens transports sperm during ejaculation
- Seminal vesicles and prostate add fluids to make semen
- Semen contains nutrients, enzymes, and alkaline buffer
- Testosterone controls male sexual characteristics
